clue.text: A gangster with means, whatever the circumstances

blocks.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster, so a gangster can be called Al
ways and means are both methods

explanation.surface: A mobster who has money to spend, come what may.
explanation.walkthrough: AL + WAYS. Al Capone, the Chicago mobster, is why crosswords so often clue AL as a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something always means doing it at every time and in every situation, an idiom matching the whole phrase.

clue.text: Tincture for an archbishop based on a holy book

indicators.note: in a down clue, the item based on another stands on top of it

blocks.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
taken as written
NUM is the abbreviation for the Book of Numbers in the Bible

explanation.surface: A medicinal tincture prescribed for a churchman, drawn from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: William Laud, Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I, is a crossword regular; the Bible's books have standard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudanum is an alcoholic solution of opium, a classic example of a medicinal tincture.

clue.text: Language of Scotsman supporting Christian martyr

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that is supporting another sits underneath it

blocks.note: St Alban is honoured as the first British Christian martyr
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: The tongue spoken by a Scot who backs a saint who died for his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: St Alban gives his name to the city of St Albans, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Albanian is the national tongue of Albania, an Indo-European language with its own branch.

clue.text: They explain the results of liquefaction

blocks.note: first meaning: answers that resolve problems
second meaning: liquids made by dissolving substances

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a science lesson, but 'explain' and 'liquefaction' point to two different senses of one plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers to puzzles and dissolved mixtures in chemistry share this plural noun, two unrelated everyday senses.

clue.text: Old raider's terms a boy rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the words before it are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: names are terms for things
Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A Viking's conditions turned down by a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: NAMES + RON, all read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were the Scandinavian Vikings who raided the coasts of Europe in early medieval times.

clue.text: Central base for cavalry, in Darlington originally?

definitions.text: Central base for cavalry, in Darlington originally?

blocks.note: surface reading: a headquarters for horse soldiers
setter's reading: the London headquarters of the police, the people who arrive like the cavalry, imagined as having started elsewhere

explanation.surface: A regimental depot for horsemen, said to have begun in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling for the cavalry means summoning rescuers; for the Metropolitan Police that call goes to its headquarters. Darlington is a market town in County Durham, nearer Scotland than London is; the exact joke is not fully clear.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the headquarters building of London's Metropolitan Police, the central command for its officers.

clue.text: Wise king willingly accepted many an honour

indicators.note: a word that has accepted others takes them inside itself

blocks.note: as in 'I would as soon go', meaning as willingly
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A sage monarch gladly took on many a distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soon' for willingly survives in phrases like 'I'd sooner not' and 'I'd as soon stay home'.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon of Israel is the Bible's byword for wisdom, famous for his judgement over two mothers.

clue.text: A monkey smashed some in a trading centre

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into bits that can be put back in a new order
places the shuffled letters inside the following word

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A monkey wrecked a few things in a marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmosets are small South American primates, a kind of monkey with clawed fingers and long tails.

clue.text: Northern cricket side with taste perhaps for absurdity

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for northern
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
taste is one example of the five senses

explanation.surface: A cricket team from the north of England with flair, ready for something silly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on, or leg, side.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense is talk or behaviour that makes no sense, a straight synonym for something ridiculous.

clue.text: Beaver gets downstream to skirt border

blocks.note: beaver is a type of animal pelt used in clothing
downstream means further below on a river

explanation.surface: A beaver swims downriver to go round the edge of its territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like a verb meaning go around; it is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a pleated flounce or ruffle trimming the hem of a dress, hence a decorative skirt edging.

clue.text: Highly ornate old penny replaced by new coin

indicators.note: one thing replaced by another is swapped out for it in the word

blocks.note: florid means elaborately decorated
d was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fancy antique penny is swapped for a modern coin.
explanation.walkthrough: FLORID with its D, the old penny, swapped for N. The florin was a British two-shilling coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a British silver two-shilling piece, and earlier a gold coin of Florence.

clue.text: Very attractive mesh fabric used in witchcraft

indicators.note: something used in another thing is put inside it

blocks.note: witchcraft is magic
net is a fabric of open mesh

explanation.surface: A gorgeous see-through material is employed in casting spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive' reads as good-looking, but the definition is literal: like a magnet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something magnetic draws people as a magnet draws iron, so it is strongly appealing or alluring.

clue.text: Little devil got up? No right to take advantage

indicators.note: 'no' says the following item is absent, so it is struck out

blocks.note: an imp is a small demon
rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A mischievous child up out of bed has no business exploiting others.
explanation.walkthrough: IMP + ROSE without its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose on someone is to exploit their good nature, unfairly making demands on them.

clue.text: Taking up point made after a party

indicators.note: something made is constructed, so the letters are built into a new form
puts the rebuilt letters behind the following words

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Raising a matter at a celebration, once the guests have gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Adopting a cause or a child is accepting it as your own, so adoption is the act of embracing something.

clue.text: It may be pulled out by a manual worker

definitions.text: It may be pulled out by a manual worker

blocks.clueFragment: pulled out by a manual worker
blocks.note: surface reading: something a labourer extracts, such as a nail or a tooth
setter's reading: a manual is a keyboard of a church instrument, and its player draws knobs to choose sounds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual worker' looks like a labourer, but an organist plays the manuals, the keyboards played by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ stop is a knob drawn out by the organist to bring a set of pipes into play.

clue.text: Rhetorical address to soldiers may be inauspicious

definitions.note: a phrase describing a noun: a sign that may be bad

blocks.note: O is the vocative cry used in rhetoric, as in 'O Romeo'
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A grand speech to the troops could be a bad sign.
explanation.walkthrough: O + MEN, as a general might cry 'O men!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent can foretell good or bad fortune, so this sign of the future may well be unlucky.

clue.text: Musical comedy about the English race works

indicators.note: a word about others goes round them

blocks.note: opera is the plural of opus, a work
E is the abbreviation for English
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A comic musical concerning a sporting contest in England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tourist Trophy motorcycle races are held each year on the Isle of Man; opera is the plural of opus.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera with spoken dialogue and comic plot, the forerunner of the stage musical.

clue.text: Unfortunate collapse for a mollusc

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters are out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad tumble for a shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Escallop is an old spelling of scallop, a bivalve shellfish with a ridged fan-shaped shell.

clue.text: Student abandons old writing instrument — it's an eyesore

indicators.note: one who abandons something walks out of it, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
a style was a pointed tool for writing on wax tablets

explanation.surface: A pupil gives up an antique pen because it looks hideous.
explanation.walkthrough: STYLE without its L. 'Eyesore' normally means an ugly sight; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sty is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a sore on the eye in the most literal sense.

clue.text: Artefacts remain in a rut perhaps? On the contrary

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters are only one possible version, so they can be rearranged
one thing in another sits inside it
says the order is the other way round, so the outer and inner words swap roles

blocks.note: to stay is to remain
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Antiques stuck in a routine, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says remain goes in a rut; 'on the contrary' flips it so the shuffled A RUT goes inside STAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is sculpture collectively, a set of carved or cast figures, which are made objects of art.

clue.text: Output, surely, of the present solver

indicators.note: an output is a product, so the letters that follow are worked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The product, without doubt, of whoever is reading this.
explanation.walkthrough: The present solver is the person reading the clue, addressed directly.
explanation.definitionFit: The person now solving is the reader, addressed in the second person by this reflexive pronoun.

clue.text: Vehicle obtained to follow French art course in Paris

indicators.note: the first items must come after the next, setting the order of the parts

blocks.note: 'tu es' is French for 'thou art'
a car is a vehicle
got means obtained

explanation.surface: A student acquires a car to take up a French art class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old verb, as in 'thou art', not painting; 'course' is a part of a meal, not a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots are snails cooked in garlic butter, a classic dish served in a French restaurant meal.

clue.text: Unchangeable, this triangle?

definitions.note: the word that completes the phrase with 'triangle'

blocks.note: first meaning: lasting for ever, never altering
second meaning: the word that goes before triangle in the phrase for a love affair between three people

explanation.walkthrough: The eternal triangle is two people in love with the same third person, an enduring story in fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting cannot alter, and the phrase for a three-way love affair begins with this word.

clue.text: Publisher's employee runs after a novelist

indicators.note: places the first item behind the following one

blocks.note: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A publishing staffer chases after a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: READE + R.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's reader assesses manuscripts to judge whether they are worth publishing, a job title in the trade.

clue.text: Change properties of article held between teeth

indicators.note: something held between other things is gripped inside them

blocks.note: a denture is a set of false teeth
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dentist's chemistry lesson: an object clamped in the jaws alters its nature.
explanation.walkthrough: A inside DENTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To denature a substance such as protein or alcohol is to alter its natural chemical character.

clue.text: Able people in capital entertainment

indicators.note: the letters wanted lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Skilled performers taking part in shows in the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Talent can mean gifted individuals collectively, as when a scout looks for new talent.

clue.text: A biblical scoffer living off the workers?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for an animal

blocks.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament
to scoff is to gobble food

explanation.surface: A Pharisee mocks a parasite who exploits the working class.
explanation.walkthrough: A + NT + EATER. 'Scoffer' suggests mockery but here means a glutton; worker ants are the 'workers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anteaters feed on ants, and worker ants are the insects that do a colony's labour, hence a political joke.

clue.text: Dismayed when a quiet friend conducted

blocks.note: taken as written
p is piano, the musical direction for soft
a pal is a friend
led means guided or conducted

explanation.surface: Upset because a quiet mate took charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To be appalled is to be shocked and horrified, a stronger version of being upset or distressed.

clue.text: Be effective — fall away to leeward

blocks.note: first meaning: to bring a good return or succeed
second meaning: the sailing term for a ship's head turning away from the wind

explanation.walkthrough: Leeward is the side sheltered from the wind; in old seamanship, a ship's head that falls off to leeward is said to pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort that succeeds pays off, and sailors use the same phrasal verb for a bow swinging downwind.
